solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Yankee maybe goes around touching cap

indicators.note: the bet goes around the other piece, enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a yankee is a kind of multiple bet on horse races, so it is an example of a bet
touching, in the sense of concerning, is RE

explanation.surface: An American, perhaps, walks round tipping their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' suggests an American, but a yankee is also a combination wager of four selections on British racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a soft round flat cap, the kind worn by soldiers or artists.

clue.text: Refuses to touch pasty, something most rare

parts.note: trade unions black goods when they refuse to handle them
wan means pale, pasty-faced

explanation.surface: Someone declines to eat a Cornish pastry, a rare thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' reads as the pastry; it is the adjective, pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A black swan was proverbially a thing that does not exist, hence any rarity.

clue.text: Reflected about opening bank account

indicators.note: as in a mirror, so the construction is read backwards
the abbreviation cuts the bank open and sits inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank of seats
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Thinking about opening a bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: A récit is a narrative, especially a recitative or a story told, so an account.

clue.text: Waves finally at vessel carrying a friend across Channel

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the little word is used
the ship holds the French phrase aboard

parts.note: SS denotes a steamship
in France, across the English Channel, a friend is un ami

explanation.surface: Waves at a ship ferrying a friend over to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge sea waves caused by earthquakes.

clue.text: Dig this good dance party album: the very thing!

parts.note: a rave is a large all-night dance party
LP, long-player, is a vinyl album
IT can mean the ideal thing, as in 'that's it!'

explanation.surface: An invitation to enjoy a good party and its soundtrack, the perfect thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig this' reads as slang for 'enjoy this', but Dig is a noun: an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravel pit is a quarry excavated for stones, so it is a kind of dig.

clue.text: Again, rely on ignoring the odd miss?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are skipped and the even ones kept

explanation.surface: Can you count on someone again who disregards an occasional failure?
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Scaled down demands of orthographer, etc

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters run within the words read downwards

explanation.surface: A spelling expert's requirements, reduced, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scaled down' sounds like reduced; it signals letters inside the phrase, read down.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc, short for et cetera, means and the rest.

clue.text: To stop the rot in political party Frenchwoman secures backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so everything is read from the end
the Frenchwoman holds the party within her

parts.note: Mme is the abbreviation for Madame
Lab is short for Labour

explanation.surface: A French politician props up a failing party to halt decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalming preserves a corpse from decay.

clue.text: Principal gutted as newspaper's staff are sacked

indicators.note: with its insides removed, only the first and last letters remain

parts.note: journalists work under the editor, so they are under ed

explanation.surface: A head teacher is devastated when a paper's staff lose their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacked a city means pillaged it, stripped it of goods.

clue.text: One enormous purse, perhaps, you might pick up

indicators.note: picking up by ear: the word as heard

parts.note: to purse lips is to tighten them, one example of tightening

explanation.surface: A huge purse that a passer-by might grab.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, from the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Got up from a cot, cured, miraculously

indicators.note: something done miraculously is transformed, so these letters change into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient rises from a sickbed, healed by a miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: Got up in the sense of dressed or kitted out; accoutred means equipped with clothing and gear.

clue.text: Chief impact of old British spy changing sides

indicators.note: left swaps over to right: the L of the spy's name is replaced by R

parts.note: Anthony Blunt, art historian and one of the Cambridge spies for the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: The main effect of a traitor defecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' looks like defection, but it swaps L (left) for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: The brunt of something is the main force of a blow or shock.

clue.text: Shelf containing note about wheels for assembly

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole construction runs backwards
the shelf holds the note within it

parts.note: a rack is a shelf or frame for storing things
TI is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions about a shelf with a note on putting wheels on.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit car is a vehicle sold in parts for the buyer to build, so a set of wheels to put together.

clue.text: Arrived in large numbers — if casually late

definitions.meaning: came pouring in, like money or waves
turned up unhurriedly after the appointed time

explanation.surface: Guests flooded in, though some strolled up after the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both arriving in a steady stream and turning up late without concern.

clue.text: Comes to get garages refurbished

indicators.note: done up afresh, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Somebody comes round to have garages done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to' suggests waking; it means totals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that comes to a sum totals it, and aggregates is a verb for amounting to.

clue.text: Old statesman to stand up in grand fashion

parts.note: an argument that will not wash does not stand up to scrutiny
G is short for grand, a thousand
ton is an old word for high fashion, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: A former politician rises to speak in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand up' suggests rising, but WASH means hold up as believable.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington, first US president, is a statesman of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: A white and gold bird found in South Eastern sierra

indicators.note: the metal and bird sit within the compass letters

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a tern is a seabird
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A white-and-gold bird spotted in mountains in the southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' looks like the bird's colour; it is a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Our second city councillor finally coming in behind

indicators.note: the letter enters the word for backside

parts.note: bum is British slang for the buttocks

indicators.note: only the closing letter of councillor is used

explanation.surface: A local council member arrives last at a Midlands town hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Brum is the nickname for Birmingham, often called Britain's second city.

clue.text: Mexicans going by balloon: and why not?

indicators.note: one piece goes beside the other in order

parts.note: the Maya are a people of southern Mexico
to balloon is to swell

explanation.surface: Mexicans travel by hot-air balloon: a suggestion met with a shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying one may as well do something means there is no reason not to.

clue.text: Don gets early round in for singer

indicators.note: the round sits within the word for don

parts.note: to don clothes is to wear them
a heat is a preliminary round of a race

explanation.surface: An Oxford don gets the first drinks in for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests a university fellow; it is the verb, put on. 'singer' is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird of open country.

clue.text: Something often common seen in pre-1945 Manhattan?

definitions.meaning: a part of speech often classed as common rather than proper
before 1945 New York had no United Nations, founded that year and later headquartered in Manhattan

explanation.surface: A question about what was ordinary in wartime New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: before 1945 there was NO UN in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar classes these words as common or proper, so a word that is often common.

clue.text: Very badly twisted bearing corroded — then left

indicators.note: the twisted word carries the other pieces within it

parts.note: wry means bent or distorted
etched means eaten away, as by acid

explanation.surface: A mechanic's report on a ruined, rusty machine part, then abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a machine part; here it means carrying, with 'then' joining the corroded and left pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretchedly means miserably or terribly, so in a very poor manner.

clue.text: Dramatist's outspoken appeal to those about to pray?

indicators.note: spoken out loud: the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: appeal to those about to pray
parts.note: a call to worshippers to go down on their knees, O kneel

explanation.surface: A playwright's outspoken plea to a congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was an American playwright, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: One protected from being fired retired with new self esteem

parts.note: someone retired for the night is in bed
ego is one's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A worker shielded from dismissal leaves with renewed confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Daniel, Abednego, with Shadrach and Meshach, survived the fiery furnace; 'fired' suggests sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the biblical figure saved from burning in Nebuchadnezzar's furnace.

clue.text: One keeping mum, possibly, after turning up concealed bug

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pa, a father, may keep a mum as his partner
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A discreet informant, revealed, planted a hidden listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping mum' suggests silence and 'bug' a microphone; the bug is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a sap-sucking insect such as a greenfly, so a bug.

clue.text: Departs with perfect set of exam results for the City

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
top grades in every subject: all A's

explanation.surface: A student with straight top grades leaves for a career in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial centre, but here it is any city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas.

clue.text: Drunk conspicuous after dark?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for tipsy and also means illuminated by lights.

clue.text: One minded attraction being withdrawn

indicators.note: drawn backwards, so the letters are reversed; the run of letters inside withdrawn itself is a coincidence

parts.note: a draw is a crowd-pulling attraction

explanation.surface: A minder's attraction to someone is being pulled back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a person, often a child, under the care of a guardian.

clue.text: What's inside leading Asian capital

indicators.note: only the inner letters of the first word are used

parts.note: number one, NO I, is the one in the lead

explanation.surface: A question about what lies within a major Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Something with element of wood, not of earth, let out

parts.note: teak is a hard tropical timber
ET is an extra-terrestrial, a being not from this planet

indicators.note: let out, the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle about elements: wood, but not earth, released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' suggests the classical elements wood and earth; it is a heating element.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle for boiling water usually heats it with an electric element.

clue.text: Recording conducted in which nothing's made public

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: the noughts go inside the word for conducted

parts.note: led means guided or conducted
read as O's, plural of O for nothing

explanation.surface: A recorded session where nothing was revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclosed means revealed, made known to others.

clue.text: Traveller accompanying Venezuelan for the drive back

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
Venezuelans speak Spanish, in which 'the' is el

explanation.surface: A salesman rides with a South American companion on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive back' suggests a car journey home; it means repulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to force them away, to repulse them.
